summary: Fixed the limitation the previous interpretation recorded: the sweep's configuration events no longer act on a configured-but-absent participant. Nodes 1..4 are now real raft instances whose stored ConfState pins voters to {1,2,3}; the network is built from 1..3 through newNetwork (whose peer branch rewrites trackers and would otherwise install all four nodes as voters, hiding the change under test) and node 4 is registered directly in the network peer map, so it starts outside the configuration but answers when a ConfChange adds it; the persist/apply loop now covers 1..4 and hands committed EntryConfChangeV2 entries to applyConfChange on node 4 too, so it can be added as a learner, promoted to a voter, or removed and re-added, and the four invariant checks include its committed index. Draft-side this revision reports seeds=60, steps_per_seed=60, elections=460, ordinary proposals=461, conf_change_proposals=335, violations=0, so still no witness now that a genuinely new participant is in the event set - but that is construction feedback only, so a fresh isolated execution of these bytes is requested, with the change in the event set recorded as the revision reason. Still outside the event set and therefore still open in gap 984747de5ed94b4ea8f6977b2a92808f-gap-2: joint-transition and learner-promotion-of-an-existing-voter proposals, node restarts that must carry the applied ConfState forward, and the liveness witness for the campaign guard's applied-lag condition.
